script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Morning, Sarah. October 22nd, 2026. Can you believe it's already this late in the year?
script.ja: おはようございます、サラさん。2026年10月22日。もうこんなに年末が近いなんて信じられますか？

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Morning, Alex. Yeah, it goes fast. Feels like yesterday we were talking about summer plans.
script.ja: おはよう、アレックス。うん、早いね。つい昨日、夏休みの計画を話してた気がする。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Tell me about it. My kid's almost a year and a half. Time just flies. Anyway, I need coffee. Really need coffee this morning.
script.ja: 全くですよ。うちの子ももう1歳半近くです。時間が経つのが早すぎます。とにかく、コーヒーが要りますね。今朝は本当にコーヒーが必要だ。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Sounds like you had a long night. I've got my tea here. Have you checked the weather?
script.ja: 長い夜だったみたいね。私は紅茶で。天気は見た？

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Not yet. I was still half asleep. Is it gonna rain?
script.ja: まだです。まだ半分寝てました。雨降りますか？

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: No rain today, actually. It's overcast, but zero percent chance of rain. High around 18, low around 11. Not bad for late October.
script.ja: いや、今日は雨は降らないみたい。曇りだけど、降水確率はゼロパーセント。最高気温が18度くらいで、最低が11度くらい。10月後半にしては悪くないね。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Oh, that’s good. I hate carrying an umbrella if I don't have to. You know, I saw something about a new giant Gundam statue going up in Tokyo this fall. Did you see that?
script.ja: おお、それは良いですね。持たなくていいなら傘は持ちたくないです。そういえば、この秋に東京に新しい巨大なガンダム像ができるって見ました？

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: I did. Another one. People really love those, don't they?
script.ja: 見たよ。また新しいのがね。みんな本当に好きなのね、ああいうの。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: They do. It's pretty amazing to see in person. I remember seeing the one in Odaiba years ago. My little one is probably too young for it, but maybe someday.
script.ja: そうですね。実物を見ると結構すごいですよ。何年か前に台場にあったのを見たのを覚えています。うちの子にはまだ早すぎるでしょうけど、いつかね。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: My son definitely would have liked it when he was younger. He was very into robots.
script.ja: うちの息子はもっと小さい頃だったら絶対喜んだと思う。ロボットに夢中だったから。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Yeah, I'm already thinking about what toys my kid will get into. It's really important to foster their interests, isn't it? Like, that's paramount.
script.ja: ええ、うちの子がどんなおもちゃに興味を持つか、もう考えてます。興味を育むのって本当に重要ですよね？なんていうか、それが一番肝心、というか。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Paramount just means 'most important.' Yes, it is important to encourage what they like.
script.ja: Paramountは「最も重要な」って意味ね。うん、好きなことを奨励するのは大事だよ。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Right, paramount. Thanks. It's just sometimes I have a hunch that I should be doing more.
script.ja: そう、パラマウント。ありがとうございます。ただ、時々、もっと何かするべきなんじゃないかって、直感があるんですよね。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: A hunch is like a strong feeling or an intuition. Don't worry too much. You're doing fine.
script.ja: Hunchは強い感覚とか直感みたいなものね。あんまり心配しすぎなくていいよ。ちゃんとやってる。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: ...Yeah. Did you see that news about a clothing company making mobile game character costumes?
script.ja: …ええ。携帯ゲームのキャラクター衣装を作る服の会社の話、見ましたか？

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: I did. Nutte and Axel Mark. It sounds like a lot of work to make those costumes for real.
script.ja: 見たよ。NutteとAxel Markね。あの衣装を実物で作るのって大変そうね。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: I'm sure it is. Some of those designs are so complicated. But people love dressing up as their favorite characters. I don't really get it myself, but my younger sister is really into cosplay.
script.ja: そうでしょうね。デザインがすごく複雑なものもありますし。でも、みんなお気に入りのキャラクターの格好をするのが好きですよね。僕自身はあんまりわからないんですけど、妹はコスプレに夢中です。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: My daughter and her friends like to do it too. Not full-on cosplay, but they wear parts of outfits. It's fun for them.
script.ja: うちの娘も友達とそういうことするよ。本格的なコスプレってわけじゃないけど、衣装の一部を着たりね。彼女たちには楽しいみたい。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Right. Speaking of design, there was that story about Keisuke Unosawa. Making the ordinary extraordinary, without a design school background.
script.ja: そうですね。デザインといえば、宇野澤啓介さんの話がありましたね。デザイン学校の経歴なしに、普通なものを特別なものにするっていう。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: That was an interesting one. It's good to hear stories like that. Shows that passion and a different perspective can really lead to something unique.
script.ja: あれは面白かったわ。ああいう話を聞くのはいいことね。情熱と異なる視点が本当にユニークなものにつながるってことを示してる。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Yeah. Sometimes it feels like you need all the right qualifications for everything. But maybe it's more about just doing it.
script.ja: そうですね。いつも何でもちゃんとした資格が必要な気がします。でも、多分、それよりもただやってみることの方が大事なんでしょうね。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: I think so. Anyway, before we finish up today's The Daily Tanu-chan Show, I just remembered, tomorrow is 電信電話記念日. Telegraph and Telephone Memorial Day.
script.ja: 私もそう思う。そういえば、今日のThe Daily Tanu-chan Showが終わる前に思い出したんだけど、明日は電信電話記念日なんだよ。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Oh, is it? What's that for?
script.ja: ああ、そうなんですか？何の日ですか？

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: It commemorates the start of Japan's first public telegraph line construction between Tokyo and Yokohama in 1869. So, October 23rd marks that. It was established by Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Public Corporation.
script.ja: 1869年に東京と横浜の間で日本初の公衆電信線の架設工事が始まったことを記念する日なの。だから、10月23日がその日。日本電信電話公社によって制定されたんだ。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Wow, 1869. That's a long time ago. Imagine a world without phones, or even telegraphs for that matter. Makes you think.
script.ja: へえ、1869年ですか。ずいぶん昔ですね。電話もない世界、いや、電信すらない世界を想像すると、考えさせられますね。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: It does. Well, that's it for today, Alex. Have a good one.
script.ja: そうだね。じゃあ、今日はここまで、アレックス。良い一日を。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: You too, Sarah. See you tomorrow.
script.ja: サラさんも。また明日。
